• Now what?
• It's sitting on your laptop doing nothing.

content.title: Serialization (Pickling)
content.explanation:
• Before you can deploy a model, you have to save it.
• You don't want to re-train the model every time the server starts!
• In Python, saving a trained model object to a file is called Serialization.
• The two most common tools for this are: 1.
• Pickle: The standard Python serialization library.

content.title: Model Deployment: From Lab to Production
content.explanation:
A model on your laptop is useless to a business. Deployment is the process of taking your trained model and making it available to the outside world.

Usually, this involves saving the model to a file, loading it onto a cloud server, and wrapping it in an API (Application Programming Interface). When an app sends data to the API, the model makes a prediction and sends it back in milliseconds.

challenge.question: Use the `joblib` library to save a trained model to your hard drive, then load it back into memory.
challenge.starterCode:
import joblib
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

model = LogisticRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# TODO: Save the model to a file named 'model.pkl'


# TODO: Load the model from 'model.pkl' into a new variable called loaded_model
loaded_model =
challenge.solution:
import joblib
# Save
joblib.dump(model, 'model.pkl')

# Load
loaded_model = joblib.load('model.pkl')
challenge.explanation: Serialization (Pickling) converts your model's learned weights into a byte-stream file. You can email this file to a colleague or upload it to a server, and they can load the exact same brain.

stages.title: The API Dilemma
stages.description: Your Model is deployed on a cloud server via a Flask API. It processes loan applications. Suddenly, the API crashes because a user submitted a loan application where their 'Age' was 'Twenty-Five' instead of 25. What is the fundamental issue?

choices.text: The model was trained for too long and overfit.
choices.outcome: Overfitting affects prediction accuracy, not software crashes.

choices.text: The API lacks input data validation. Models expect strict numerical formats, not strings.
choices.outcome: Exactly! In production, you must validate and clean incoming API data to match the exact format the model was trained on.

choices.text: The cloud server doesn't have enough RAM.
choices.outcome: While RAM is important, a single string input causing a crash is a type mismatch error, not a memory error.
